original_question: Let L and M be elliptic, second-order, selfadjoint, strictly positive Dirichlet operators in a bounded domain D subset R^n with n > 1 and smooth connected boundary S. Assume the coefficients of L and M are real-valued, and let a(x) and b(x) be strictly positive functions smooth on the closure of D. If real-valued functions u and v satisfy Lu + a(x)v = 0 in D, -b(x)u + Mv = 0 in D, and u = v = 0 on S, does it necessarily follow that u = v = 0 in D, without adding any further assumptions such as L = M or smallness of |b - a|?

The paper explicitly says that all functions under discussion are real-valued; your draft enforces this for u and v, but the paper states it as part of the overall setup arising from the real-valued coefficients.
For full paper-faithfulness, it helps to mention the nearby context that the one-dimensional analogue is already known to have an affirmative answer, so the open problem is genuinely for n > 1.
refined_question: Determine whether the following statement is true or false, without imposing any additional hypotheses such as L = M, smallness of |b - a|, or similar side conditions: let D be a bounded domain in R^n, n > 1, with smooth connected boundary S. Let L and M be elliptic, second-order, selfadjoint, strictly positive Dirichlet operators in D with real-valued coefficients, so that all functions involved are real-valued, and let a(x), b(x) be strictly positive functions smooth on the closure of D. If real-valued functions u and v satisfy Lu + a(x)v = 0 in D, -b(x)u + Mv = 0 in D, and u = v = 0 on S, must it follow that u = v = 0 in D? If not, construct a counterexample.

The final sentence of the section on page 2 adds that the one-dimensional case is already known to have a positive answer, confirming that the intended open problem is the case n > 1.
